result.rationale: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the full SafeParseResult object (refreshTokenResponse), not .data. GoogleCalendarService.ts diff shows `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema); await prisma.credential.update({ data: { key } })`, persisting the {success, data} wrapper instead of the previously parsed googleCredentialSchema value. The stored shape lacks top-level access_token, breaking subsequent credential loads.

judged_text: GoogleCalendarService persists parseRefreshTokenResponse's return value — the entire zod SafeParseResult ({success, data}) — directly as Credential.key, replacing the previous googleCredentialSchema.parse(googleCredentials) value. Every Google Calendar token refresh on the default configuration (credential sync disabled) writes {success:true, data:{...}} into the credential row; on the next load getGoogleAuth reads credential.key, finds no top-level access_token/refresh_token, and throws, permanently breaking the user's Google Calendar integration and every booking that uses it until the app is reinstalled — the stored wrapper shape is unreadable by the app.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the refresh logic was changed from `googleCredentialSchema.parse(googleCredentials)` (which returns the parsed credential object) to `parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema)` and the result is persisted directly as `Credential.key` (`data: { key }`). But `parseRefreshTokenResponse` (new file `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`) returns the Zod `safeParse` result object (`{ success, data, ... }`), not `refreshTokenResponse.data`. Persisting that wrapper shape would replace the credential key object with an unreadable structure for code expecting top-level `access_token`, `refresh_token`, etc., matching the finding’s described breakage.
